summary: A landowner pays the last hired the same as the first, and asks whether his goodness is a cause for resentment.

context.title: Labourers in the vineyard
paragraphs: Matthew alone records this parable, placed between two sayings about the last being first. [c1] The owner’s closing question uses the Jewish idiom of the evil eye. [c2]

translationNotes.summary: Greek asks “is your eye evil?”, an idiom for begrudging another’s good.
translationNotes.body: The evil eye was a familiar image for stinginess and resentment (Deut 15:9). [c2] English trades the image for an abstract feeling. [c2]

claims.text: The parable of the labourers in the vineyard appears only in Matthew.
An “evil eye” was a Jewish idiom for stinginess or begrudging another’s good.

sources.citation: A commentary page written for the bad-week fixture
